contract.description: Generate a Mitsubishi GX Works2 list-format PROGRAM CSV (FX2/FX3) from structured rungs. contract.description:
Use: Generate and validate one complete LAD (ladder) XML plan, V16-V21; V19+ uses V18 XML.
When: Supply plan plus output_path/output_directory for a file; callee_interfaces for calls; classic CPUs need target_family/block_number.
Avoid: Invented pins, TEMP timer state or hand-spliced FlgNet. timer static type=TON_TIME; global DB calls need instance.scope=GlobalVariable.
Next: Review logicSummary; resolve unknown pins with instruction_spec. contact_coil is OR(branches) AND contacts. Import/compile/save only within scope; no output path means no file.

boxPort.description: Named {port,operand}; positional {operand} or direct operand fields.

branch.description: One complete leg inside the leading OR group, not the whole group. A seal-in needs two branch objects: Start and the output's own hold contact.

branches.description: Nested OR before this leg's contacts. Children repeat this contacts/branches shape. Each OR needs at least 2 legs; runtime validates recursive children.

kind.description: coil (default), set_coil, reset_coil, negated_coil (assign NOT power). Edge and timer/counter coils unsupported.

negated.description: true tests NOT operand; false tests operand. Follow the signal's actual polarity.

direction.description: Wire in (default)/out; outputs require explicit out. IN_OUT: in + section=InOut, or callee_interfaces.inout.

inputSchema.description: Supply plan (complete object, preferred) or plan_json (JSON string). At least one non-empty plan is required.

block_number.description: Optional top-level alias for plan.block_number. Classic S7-300/400 FB/FC blocks need a fixed number.

output_path.description: Set a workspace XML path on the first call when the result will be imported, read back or delivered as a file. Omitted: XML is returned only, no file is created.

plan.description: Complete block: block_name, block_type, schema_version, interface, networks. Operands: variable {name,scope?} or constant {constant_value,datatype}, no name needed for constants; scope defaults to LocalVariable. Member comments are accepted but not emitted (warning).

block.description: Legacy wrapper accepted for compatibility: block.name/block.type/block.number or block.autoNumber.

block_name.description: Target OB/FB/FC block name, for example Main or FB_Motor.

block_number.description: Fixed block number; required for S7-300/400, optional for optimized targets.

block_type.description: OB (ProgramCycle only), FB or FC. OB: Temp/Constant only.

callee_interfaces.description: Map call_name -> {input,output,inout:[{name,datatype}]}; infers Section/Type and checks members. Reuse known interfaces; export an existing callee only if unknown.

comment.description: Accepted, not emitted (warning). Use networks[].comment or write_object_attributes on the real block.

culture.description: Network text language; default zh-CN. Must exist in target project or import fails.

interface.description: PLC block interface. Canonical keys are input/output/inout/static_members/temp/constant. Legacy inputs/outputs/static are also accepted and normalized.

networks.description: contact_coil: branches -> contacts -> coil. fb_call/move/instruction_box: optional enable. timer: TON/TOF/TP/TONR. chain: ordered boxes. Legacy elements normalize to contact_coil.

box_inputs.description: Use {port,operand} for named pins, or operands in the instruction's DATA pin order. en uses enable. Query instruction_spec when the needed pin order is unknown.

box_outputs.description: Use {port,operand} for named pins or positional operands. CTU positional #0 is Q; port CV selects CV. Outputs require writable variables.

branches.description: Leading OR group, at least 2 legs. Three alternative paths require three branch objects; top-level contacts do not add another parallel path.

contacts.description: AND after branches: (OR of branch legs) AND every contact here. Put common permissives here; each independent start/hold/jog path belongs in branches. Choose negation from signal meaning.

equation.description: Required for Calc: formula using IN1..INn, e.g. (IN1-IN2)/IN3.

fanout.description: chain: last stage's power-out (or enable with no stages) drives every sink on one wire. Sink: coil {operand,mode?} or box {part_name,box_inputs?,box_outputs?}.

instance.description: Required for FB instructions. Two legal homes: {name} (scope LocalVariable default; an FB plan auto-declares the missing Static member) or {name, scope:"GlobalVariable"} backed by a real single-instance DB.

stages.description: chain: ordered {part_name,box_inputs?,box_outputs?,version?} boxes, each with power-in/out. Stage k's power-out feeds stage k+1's power-in; each has independent data wiring. Pin shapes match instruction_box.

type.description: contact_coil, fb_call, move, timer, instruction_box or chain.

schema_version.description: V16-V21; V16-V18 native XML, V19-V21 V18-format XML. Omitted follows project/live target, else V18. V15 requires real exported V15 XML.

target_family.description: S7-300/400 require classic XML attributes and explicit block_number; S7-1200/1500 use optimized XML (default). Pass the actual CPU family.

title.description: Accepted, not emitted (warning). Use networks[].title or write_object_attributes on the real block.

plan_json.description: Stringified fallback of plan. Prefer the plan object form: stringified JSON double-encodes and truncates on long plans.

target_family.description: Optional top-level alias for plan.target_family. Accepts S7-300, S7-400, S7-1200, or S7-1500; useful when target metadata is supplied beside tia_version.

contract.description: Generate a real GRAPH (sequential function chart) FB as TIA Openness SimaticML XML from a plan of named steps. V16-V21 (machine-verified per-version stamp table): by default each step gets one following transition (Trans{k} unless overridden) and the linear Connections graph S_k -> T_k -> S_{k+1} -> ... -> EndConnection. A step's next jumps its following transition to ANY defined step (self-loop / loop-back / forward jump; a fully-looped block has no EndConnection), and a step's alternatives declares an alternative branch (>=2 competing transitions, each {transition?, condition?, next}) — the Direct/Jump LinkType is derived automatically from the import-verified rule. A step may give a condition (the following transition's condition), an interlock, and/or a supervision — each a series (AND) chain of normally-open contacts; omitted/[] leaves an empty skeleton. A step may also give actions (each a qualifier-tagged target := value assignment), and the plan may declare variables[] (block Static members) so those actions have writable targets and the block compiles clean. The fixed envelope (block AttributeList, GRAPH_BASE interface + standard GRAPH I/O parameters, PreOperations/PostOperations, AlarmsSettings, version stamps) is the import-verified golden verbatim. Writes the .xml when output_path is given (mutating); omit it to get the XML back in the result. Versions other than V16-V21 are rejected with a structured ok:false. The TIA compiler auto-generates the GRAPH runtime block on import; do not hand-write it. Condition/interlock/supervision contacts default to scope GlobalVariable: each such PLC tag must pre-exist as Bool with a bit address (create via tia_openness_create_tags first, or switch to variables[] + scope LocalVariable); the result's requiredGlobalTags field lists them. Local ok:true is shape correctness, not a TIA compile — confirm via tia_openness_import_block_xml + tia_openness_compile. Minimal plan with an action + a loop-back: {"block_name":"FB_Seq","variables":[{"name":"MyOut","datatype":"Bool"}],"steps":[{"name":"Idle","init":true,"actions":[{"qualifier":"N","target":"MyOut","value":"TRUE"}]},{"name":"Run","condition":[{"operand":"INIT_SQ","scope":"LocalVariable"}]},{"name":"Done","next":"Idle"}]}. Alternative-branch plan (2 competing transitions after Idle; each path loops back, so no EndConnection): {"block_name":"FB_Branch","variables":[{"name":"StartA","datatype":"Bool"},{"name":"StartB","datatype":"Bool"}],"steps":[{"name":"Idle","init":true,"alternatives":[{"condition":[{"operand":"StartA","scope":"LocalVariable"}],"next":"PathA"},{"condition":[{"operand":"StartB","scope":"LocalVariable"}],"next":"PathB"}]},{"name":"PathA","next":"Idle"},{"name":"PathB","next":"Idle"}]}.

action.description: One step action. The qualifier decides the form (both import-verified): N is an assignment '#target := value' (value REQUIRED); S and R are set/reset coils '#target' (value FORBIDDEN — GRAPH rejects 'S #target := value'). Only N, S, R are supported in Phase 2b; other qualifiers (L/D/CU/CD/ON/OFF/TL/TD/TF/TR/CS/CR) are rejected until their form is machine-verified. target is an identifier (letters/digits/underscore, not starting with a digit). scope is the string LocalVariable (a block Static/interface member such as a declared variable; the default when omitted, rendered as #target) or GlobalVariable (a PLC tag, rendered as "target"). A NON-ASCII target (e.g. 夹紧阀) is accepted only with scope GlobalVariable, because that form is already quoted; the bare LocalVariable form '#夹紧阀' would need a '#"…"' spelling that is not import-verified, so it is refused rather than guessed — either make it a PLC tag with GlobalVariable scope, or give the Static member an ASCII name. value (N only) is a boolean literal (TRUE/FALSE) or an integer literal — an identifier value (assigning another member/tag) needs a scoped form not yet import-verified, so it is rejected. The target must be WRITABLE — declare it in variables[]; the read-only GRAPH inputs and reserved system parameters (OFF_SQ, S_NO, etc.) are not valid variable names.

alternative.description: One competing transition of an alternative branch. transition (optional) overrides the transition name; the default is Trans{k} (k = global 1-based transition index). condition (optional) is this path's firing condition — a series (AND) chain of NO contacts; omit or [] for unconditional. next (required) is the target step NAME; the generator derives the LinkType (the target's first feed on the start-reachable flow is Direct, merges/loop-backs and any edge into the first step are Jump — both import-verified).

condition.description: This alternative's firing condition: a series (AND) chain of NO contacts. Omit or [] for unconditional.

contact.description: One normally-open (NO) series contact in a condition. operand is a simple identifier: the tag or interface-member name (letters/digits/underscore only; no dots, quotes, or brackets in Phase 2a). scope is the string GlobalVariable (a PLC global tag; the default when omitted) or LocalVariable (a block interface member such as INIT_SQ). A GlobalVariable operand MUST already exist in a PLC tag table as data type Bool WITH a bit address (e.g. %M10.0) before import — otherwise compile fails with 'Tag not defined', and a name-only tag (no address) still fails with 'The entered address does not match the data type Bool'. Either pre-create it via tia_openness_create_tags (data_type Bool + logical_address) or declare the signal in variables[] and use scope LocalVariable instead (self-contained, compiles clean); the generate result's requiredGlobalTags field lists every tag that must exist.

step.description: One sequence step. name is the step identifier (must be unique). init (optional bool) marks the initial step; when omitted it defaults to true for the FIRST step only and false for the rest. transition (optional) overrides the name of the transition that FOLLOWS this step; the default is Trans{k} (k = global 1-based transition index). condition (optional) is the condition of the transition that FOLLOWS this step; interlock/supervision (optional) are this step's interlock/supervision conditions, each a series (AND) chain of contacts; omit or use [] for an empty (unconditional) skeleton. actions (optional) are this step's actions; omit or [] for none. next (optional) jumps the following transition to a named step. alternatives (optional) replaces the single following transition with >=2 competing ones and is therefore mutually exclusive with transition/condition/next (interlock/supervision/actions still apply to the step itself).

actions.description: This step's actions. Omit or [] for none. Phase 2b supports the import-verified N/S/R qualifiers only: N is an assignment (target := value, value required), S/R are set/reset coils (target only, value forbidden). No ST expressions, function calls, events, or action interlocks.

alternatives.description: Optional alternative branch (Type AltBegin): two or more COMPETING transitions after this step — at runtime the leftmost transition whose condition fires wins. Each entry is {transition?, condition?, next} with next required. Requires at least 2 entries (a single following transition is the plain transition/condition/next form). Mutually exclusive with this step's transition/condition/next fields. Parallel (simultaneous) branches are not supported (not yet machine-verified).

condition.description: Condition for the transition that FOLLOWS this step: a series (AND) chain of normally-open (NO) contacts. Every contact must be true to fire the transition. Omit or [] for an unconditional transition. Phase 2a supports series NO contacts only (no negated/NC contacts, no parallel/OR). Each operand is one plain tag/member name; non-ASCII names (e.g. 夹紧到位) are allowed, dotted paths ("DB".Member) are not. There is no step-time condition — GRAPH's 'wait 2 s' (Step.T >= T#2s) is NOT expressible here, so drive a Bool from a TON in another block and reference that Bool.

interlock.description: This step's interlock condition (IlCoil): a series (AND) chain of NO contacts. Omit or [] for none.

name.description: Step identifier, unique in the block. Step names, transition names and variables[] names all share the GRAPH block's symbol namespace with the sequencer's reserved system parameters, so these names are rejected up front (case-insensitive): OFF_SQ, INIT_SQ, ACK_EF, S_PREV, S_NEXT, SW_AUTO, SW_TAP, SW_TOP, SW_MAN, S_SEL, S_ON, S_OFF, T_PUSH, S_NO, S_MORE, S_ACTIVE, ERR_FLT, AUTO_ON, TAP_ON, TOP_ON, MAN_ON, OFF_SQ_BASE, FAULT, ERROR, T_PREV, T_NEXT, HALT_SQ, HALT_TM, ZERO_OP, EN_IL, EN_SV, EN_ACKREQ, EN_SSKIP, DISP_SACT, G7T. The industry-standard fault-step names "Fault"/"Error" hit this — use e.g. "FaultStep"/"ErrorStep".

next.description: Optional target step NAME for the transition that FOLLOWS this step — any defined step: this step itself (self-loop), an earlier step (loop-back), or a later step (forward jump). Omitted keeps the linear flow (next defined step, or EndConnection on the last step). The connection LinkType is derived automatically from the import-verified rule (each step's first feed on the flow reachable from the first step is Direct; merges, loop-backs, and any edge into the first step are Jump) — it is never specified in the plan. Every step except the first must end up reachable from the first step's flow, or generation is rejected.

supervision.description: This step's supervision condition (SvCoil): a series (AND) chain of NO contacts. Omit or [] for none.

variable.description: One block Static member. name is an identifier (letters/digits/underscore, not starting with a digit; unique) — non-ASCII letters are allowed, so a zh-CN project can declare 夹紧阀 directly. datatype is a SimaticML datatype string such as Bool, Int, Real, Word, Time (non-empty).

block_name.description: Target GRAPH FB name, for example FB_Sequence. GRAPH blocks are always FBs.

block_number.description: Optional block number. Defaults to 1 (AutoNumber stays on).

culture.description: Project editing language for every MultilingualText/Culture stamp in the generated document, e.g. zh-CN (default) or en-US. MUST match a language that exists in the target project or TIA rejects the import ('culture does not exist within the current project'). Omit for a zh-CN project.

schema_version.description: TIA schema version: V16-V21 (all machine-verified; the per-version stamp table handles the real deltas — V16 uses Interface/v4, and V16/V17 omit the block Namespace element). Any other version is rejected with a structured ok:false (never downgraded). Omitted defaults to the project's openness_version (plc-code.project.json), else V20.

steps.description: The sequence of named steps (at least one), defined in flow order. Default topology is linear: ONE derived transition after each step, S_k -> T_k -> S_{k+1}, and T_n -> the sequence end (EndConnection). A step's next field jumps its following transition to ANY defined step instead (self-loop / loop-back / forward jump; an explicit next on the last step removes the EndConnection, so a fully-looped block has none — import-verified). A step's alternatives field declares an alternative branch: >=2 competing transitions, each with its own target. Transitions/interlocks/supervisions are empty skeletons unless a step supplies a condition/interlock/supervision; step actions are empty unless a step supplies actions. The TIA compiler auto-generates the GRAPH runtime block on import (do not hand-write it). A bare string "StepName" is also accepted as shorthand for { name: "StepName" }.

variables.description: Optional block Static members (name + datatype). Rendered into the FB's Static interface section so step actions have WRITABLE targets — the recommended, compile-safe shape is to declare a variable here and drive it from a LocalVariable action. Omit or [] to leave the Static section empty. The read-only standard GRAPH inputs (OFF_SQ, INIT_SQ, ...) are NOT writable; declare your own Static variable instead.

contract.name: tia_openness_generate_graph_block

contract.description:
Use: Validate and generate a complete SIMATIC SD FB/FC/OB plan.
When: V20/V21 authoring; output_directory writes BOM/CRLF .s7dcl + .s7res.
Avoid: Using SD on V16-V19; use LAD XML there.
Next: Resolve a concrete unsupported shape with instruction_spec; import the paired documents and obtain a final compile verdict.

binding.description: One wired parameter for an instr op: name (the catalog parameter token, e.g. REQ/ID/CONNECT) and op (the operand). Direction (:= vs =>) comes from the catalog signature, not set here. Omit a parameter to leave it unbound (renders name:=  ).

box_arg.description: Generic box param: name (param token), dir (in -> name:=op default, out -> name=>op), op (operand).

box_pragma.description: Box pragma. style single = `{ k := "v"; ... }` on one line; multi (default) = multi-line block where every entry except the last ends `; `. entries are {key, value}, value is the inner text e.g. key=S7_Templates value="SrcType := Real" or "[SrcType := Real, DestType := DInt]".

cc_branch.description: One parallel OR leg of a contact_coil network: a series chain of contacts (ANDed). The legs are ORed together. A single-contact leg is just {contacts:[{operand:{name:...}}]}.

cc_coil.description: The driven coil of a contact_coil network. operand is the tag; kind (optional) is coil (default), s_coil (set) or r_coil (reset).

cc_contact.description: A contact in the contact_coil form. operand is the tag; kind (optional) is contact/no (normally-open, default) or i_contact/nc (normally-closed).

element.description: op selects the element: contact/i_contact/coil/s_coil/r_coil (operand); wire (name, inline wire#); compare (kind in EQ/NE/GT/LT/GE/LE, in1, in2, optional src_type — inferred from interface-local operand datatypes or a constant's shape; set it explicitly when both operands are global/DB members of a non-Int type); range (kind in InRange/OutRange, min, in, max, optional src_type); move (in, outputs[] -> out1..outN); timer (kind TON/TP/TOF/TONR, instance, instance_scope local|global, optional r for TONR reset, pt, optional et); math (kind Add/Sub/Mul/Div/Mod/And/Or/Xor/Min/Max, in1, in2, out, optional src_type default Int, optional generate_eno bool); unary_math (kind Abs/Neg/Sqr/Sqrt/Round/Trunc/Ceil/Floor/Frac/Ln/Exp/Sin/Cos/Tan/Asin/Acos/Atan, in, out, optional src_type default Real, optional dest_type for Round/Trunc/Ceil/Floor default DInt); counter (kind CTU/CTD/CTUD, instance, instance_scope local|global, value_type default Int; CTU uses r/pv/cv, CTD uses ld/pv/cv, CTUD uses cd/r/ld/pv/qd/cv; pv required, qd/cv optional outputs, cu is the preceding contact RLO not a param, instance declared in var_retain as CTU_INT/CTD_INT/CTUD_INT); edge_contact (kind P rising / N falling, operand trigger, bit edge-memory Bool declared in VAR — both operand and bit render with :=); box (GENERIC function box for any LAD box instruction not covered by a typed op above — name is the instruction token e.g. Convert/Scale/Normalize/Calculate/Limit/Sel/Mux/Shl/Shr/Ror/Rol/T_ADD/string funcs; optional pragma {style single|multi, entries[{key,value}] e.g. key S7_Templates value "SrcType := Real"}; args[{name, dir in|out, op}] in order — dir in renders name:=op, out renders name=>op; correctness of an arbitrary box is proven by tia_openness_import_block_sd compile, not assumed); ONE call = exactly ONE POU: put the POU's complete network set in this single networks=[{title,instructions:[{instruction,namespace,inputs:{PORT:VARIABLE},inouts:{PORT:VARIABLE},outputs:{PORT:VARIABLE}}]}] array â€” each array element becomes one sequentially numbered network inside that POU. Use the schema and inline port tables when they cover the requested instruction. If a required pin, namespace or shape is missing or ambiguous, query codesys_lad_instruction_spec for that instruction BEFORE generating; do not invent it or repeat broad catalog searches. NATIVE OPERATOR item shape: {instruction,dataType,inputs,outputs} â€” dataType is REQUIRED and is the explicit IEC operand type (numeric types for compare/arith: SINT/USINT/INT/UINT/DINT/UDINT/LINT/ULINT/REAL/LREAL â€” NOT WORD/BYTE, so convert CTU.CV WORD first with WORD_TO_INT; bit types BOOL/BYTE/WORD/DWORD/LWORD for logic; the TARGET type for conversions, e.g. INT_TO_REAL -> dataType=REAL; MOD takes INTEGER operands only (INT-family â€” NOT REAL); real functions EXP/EXPT/LN/LOG/SIN/COS/TAN/ASIN/ACOS/ATAN/SQRT take REAL/LREAL operands only). Compare ports: IN1/IN2 -> OUT:BOOL. Logic ports: IN1/IN2 -> OUT (NOT: IN -> OUT). SEL has G:BOOL+IN0/IN1; MUX has K:DINT+IN0/IN1; LIMIT has MN/IN/MX; shifts SHL/SHR/ROL/ROR have IN=bit type (BOOL/BYTE/WORD/DWORD/LWORD)+N:DINT. Every output variable gets exactly ONE writer. Verified shapes (live catalog 2026-09-06): TON/TOF/TP inputs IN:BOOL+PT:TIME, outputs Q:BOOL+ET:TIME; CTU inputs CU:BOOL+RESET:BOOL+PV:WORD, outputs Q:BOOL+CV:WORD (Q = CV>=PV); CTD inputs CD:BOOL+LOAD:BOOL+PV:WORD, outputs Q:BOOL+CV:WORD (Q = CV=0); CTUD inputs CU/CD/RESET/LOAD:BOOL+PV:WORD, outputs QU/QD:BOOL+CV:WORD (QU = CV>=PV full, QD = CV<=0 empty â€” use these boundary outputs for æ»¡ä½/ç©ºä½ judgments); SR inputs SET1/RESET:BOOL, output Q1:BOOL (RS is NOT in the registry); R_TRIG/F_TRIG input CLK:BOOL, output Q:BOOL; BLINK inputs ENABLE:BOOL+TIMELOW:TIME+TIMEHIGH:TIME, output OUT:BOOL. Namespace is STANDARD for these FBs, UTIL for BLINK. Same-name calls fail with destination_exists (no overwrite/append) â€” use inoproshop_object_regenerate to replace. Qualified symbols (GVL.Member) REQUIRE a top-level symbolTypes map with each symbol's exact IEC type. Rules: bind ports to EXACT types (CTU/CTUD.CV is WORD â€” bind a WORD symbol); TIME literals plain single-unit (T#1s, T#500ms â€” NOT T#1s500ms); variable declarations accept IEC primitive types only; NEVER use a variables array to declare FB instances (SR/BLINK/TON...) â€” the generator auto-declares instances from the instruction/instance fields (c29 trap: declaring SR/BLINK instances as variables fails UNSUPPORTED_VARIABLE_TYPE); BLINK works OUT OF THE BOX â€” the generator auto-references the UTIL library, never call any library tool for it; the native batch does NOT accept a task field â€” wire via inoproshop_task_pou_set or inoproshop_project_finalize afterwards; ADD64_64/SUB64_64 (SM0) are practically unusable on AM600 â€” accumulate in ST with ULINT. data.acceptanceVerdict is the compilation/diagnostic verdict (pass/fail from observedErrorCount), not proof of requested control behaviour â€” exitCode/compileOk are transport noise. On lad_preexisting_diagnostics the plan is almost never at fault â€” the tool auto-flushes stale IDE diagnostics and retries once. NAMESPACE PREWARM (E2E V2 R090, measured on AM600-CPU1608TP/TN): on a freshly created project the STANDARD namespace is not registered until the project has been compiled once, so the FIRST generation of a Standard FB (R_TRIG/TON/TOF/CTU/CTD/CTUD) fails at validate_plan with SIGNATURE_SELECTOR_NOT_FOUND expected=STANDARD candidates=[]. The tool now runs ONE offline build itself and re-runs the SAME plan once; read data.namespacePrewarm = {performed, reason, build:{errorCount,warningCount,compileStatus,acceptanceVerdict}, retried, recoveredOnRetry, originalFailure}. The trigger requires EVERY reported failure to be SIGNATURE_SELECTOR_NOT_FOUND with an EMPTY candidates[] list; this does not prove that the requested instruction exists. The original errors[] remain in data.namespacePrewarm.originalFailure if the retry also fails. Read data.namespacePrewarm: do not repeat a manual compile plus unchanged generation after performed=true and retried=true. If it still fails, use the final diagnostics and originalFailure to check the requested instruction/namespace against the current live catalog. If performed=false or buildError is present, fix the reported build/environment prerequisite before retrying; an incomplete prewarm does not prove the instruction is absent.

contract.description: CANONICAL vanilla-CODESYS (SP22, CODESYS Ladder plugin) LAD generator. ONE call = ONE PROGRAM POU with the complete networks[] array (each element = one network, max 60). NETWORK TYPES - EXACT ACCEPTED SURFACE (bridge `_normalize_project_network`, measured 2026-09-10; the `type` enum in the schema below IS the complete contract: contact_coil | box | timer | counter | fb. timer and counter are SUGAR over fb - each becomes an FB-instance call with instruction+instance): (1) contact_coil - relay logic only. REQUIRED coil{target} (the bridge also accepts coil{name|value}). REQUIRED-ONE-OF contacts[] (series, each {name, negated?}; negated=true IS the NC contact and IS emitted) OR branches[] (>=2 parallel OR legs, each {contacts:[{name,negated?}]}); giving both means coil := (OR of branch legs) AND (AND of series contacts). Example: {"type":"contact_coil","contacts":[{"name":"xPermit"},{"name":"xStop","negated":true}],"coil":{"target":"xOut"}}. (2) box - ONE library FUNCTION or IEC built-in operator (a FunctionBlock here is rejected plcopen_project_box_function_only - use fb). REQUIRED instruction; outputs{PORT:target} where a built-in's output pin IS the instruction name: {"type":"box","instruction":"GT","inputs":{"IN1":"iLevel","IN2":"iSet"},"outputs":{"GT":"xHigh"}}. OPTIONAL inputs{PORT:expr} (pin names validated against the live signature), enable{name} (defaults to TRUE; becomes the EN contact), coil is rejected for box networks (plcopen_project_box_coil_unsupported); wire the result through outputs. Only ONE data output. (3) timer - REQUIRED timer (TON|TOF|TP) or instruction, instance (string or {name}), input{name} (BOOL power contact wired to the FB's FIRST input pin), pt{constant_value:"T#3s"|name}, q{name}. OPTIONAL et{name} - schema-only, NOT wired (Q only). Example: {"type":"timer","timer":"TON","instance":"tonDelay","input":{"name":"xRun"},"pt":{"constant_value":"T#3s"},"q":{"name":"xDelayDone"}}. (4) counter - REQUIRED counter (CTU|CTD|CTUD) or instruction, instance, input{name} (CU/CD power contact), pv{constant_value|name} (WORD-typed on the vanilla standard library - bind a WORD variable), q{name}. OPTIONAL reset{name}, load{name} (wired to RESET/LOAD when the signature has them), cv{name} - schema-only, NOT wired. Example: {"type":"counter","counter":"CTU","instance":"ctuParts","input":{"name":"xPartEdge"},"pv":{"name":"wTarget"},"q":{"name":"xBatchDone"}}. (5) fb - the generic FB instance, for EVERY library or project-internal FunctionBlock that is not a plain timer/counter. REQUIRED instruction, instance (string or {name}), input{name} (BOOL contact wired to the FB's FIRST input pin: CTU=CU, R_TRIG=CLK, TON=IN - a data-only FB whose first pin is not BOOL must be wrapped in an ST FUNCTION_BLOCK with a BOOL first pin), outputs{EXACTLY ONE port: target} (a second output is rejected plcopen_project_fb_single_output; that one output is emitted as a coil). OPTIONAL inputs{PORT:expr} (data pins, port names matched case-insensitively, CONSTANT LITERALS ALLOWED here - unlike generic box pins). Example: {"type":"fb","instruction":"R_TRIG","instance":"rtStart","input":{"name":"xStart"},"outputs":{"Q":"xStartEdge"}}. WHEN box/fb IS MANDATORY, NOT OPTIONAL: any time- or count-dependent behaviour (ON/OFF delay, pulse, PWM duty, batch count, totalizer), edge detection and every 'act once per press' step, comparisons (GT/GE/LT/LE/EQ/NE), arithmetic (ADD/SUB/MUL/DIV/MOD), selection (SEL/MUX/LIMIT/MIN/MAX), conversions, string functions, and EVERY user-FB or library-FB instance. NEVER emulate a timer or a counter with self-holding contacts or by counting scans: contact/coil networks have no time base and no count state, the phase drifts with the task period, and the defect is INVISIBLE at compile time (E2E V2 R053: a PWM period emulated with a self-holding contact kept running through the stop cycle - measured 347 ms against a nominal 2000 ms high time; only codesys_sim_assert exposed it; the fix was an explicit command contact in series with the seal-in leg). contact_coil is ONLY for genuinely Boolean relay logic: seal-in, interlock, permissive chain, lamp/valve drive. POU NAME: pass `name`, the required field in this tool schema. The bridge also accepts block_name/pouName internally for compatibility; use name in public calls. The name must be a non-reserved IEC identifier and must NOT equal an instruction name. READBACK COUNT SEMANTICS (E2E V2 R050): readbackCounts.coil/contact count every output line and every pin contact â€” a fb network's Q output line counts as a coil and its CLK/IN pin contact counts as a contact, so 2 contact_coil networks + 1 fb network can report coil=3 / contact=7. Compare the network SHAPE, not the raw counts. The bridge emits deterministic PLCopen TC6 XML, imports it through the Ladder plugin's own converter, then checks that native-export readback contains graphical nodes (ladderBodyVerified + readbackCounts). These fields prove node presence only, not correct wiring or requested control behaviour; use selected block readback and appropriate logic tests for those claims â€” a clean compile alone is NOT proof of a real LAD body. IMPORT LOCATION (E2E V1 R036 false-green trap): the POU lands in the resolved device Application node (result carries parent + importedPath) â€” never the project root, where build.compile passes 0/0/0 while the POU does not participate; pass parent only to place it elsewhere. ACCEPTANCE: ladderBodyVerified + readbackCounts AND a final whole-project compile with the POU in the task call list (codesys_task_pou_set) â€” an unreferenced POU compiles clean but never runs. TYPE CONTRACT (E2E V1 R036): CODESYS standard-library CTU/CTD/CTUD are WORD-typed â€” bind pv/cv to WORD variables (or literal values 0..65535), NOT DINT/INT. NOT GENERATABLE (verified absent on the vanilla line): SET/RESET COILS and negated coils, MOVE box, constant literals on generic box inputs, initial values on variables[] â€” use SR/RS FB networks for latches, R_TRIG/F_TRIG FB networks for edges, and SEL chains for conditional assignment. FB NETWORKS (type "fb"): a generic FunctionBlock instance â€” {instruction, instance, input:{name} (BOOL contact wired to the FIRST input pin â€” for CTU that pin is CU, i.e. the COUNT-ENABLE contact, not a power rail; for R_TRIG it is CLK; for TON it is IN), inputs:{PORT: expr} (data pins, CONSTANT LITERALS ALLOWED â€” unlike generic box pins), outputs:{FIRST_OUTPUT_PORT: target}}; ONLY the first output pin can be wired (the Ladder plugin editor rejects a second output, 2026-09-08 verified). instruction may be a library FB OR a PROJECT-INTERNAL user FB (E2E V2 R031 verified: a user FB created on the ST channel is called from LAD with this shape, 0/0) â€” this generator only creates PROGRAM POUs, so an FB-shaped deliverable means: ST channel creates the FB body, LAD fb networks instance and call it. The instance is auto-declared in the POU's local vars â€” do NOT also declare the same name in a GVL (silent duplicate). The timer/counter kinds are the SAME shape with friendlier fields. MACHINE-VERIFIED FBs (probe 2026-09-09: import + native-export readback + task call + whole-PLC 0/0): TON/TOF/TP/CTU/CTD/CTUD plus SR (SET1 bus / RESET data -> Q1), RS (SET bus / RESET1 data -> Q1), R_TRIG (CLK -> Q), F_TRIG (CLK -> Q). NOT in the local catalog (rejected before import with instruction_signature_unresolved): BLINK (the Util library is not referenced by the Standard.project template) and TONR (no signature) â€” do not plan on either. SCAN SEMANTICS (E2E V2 R024, verified 33-network shift at 0/0): coils evaluate in network order and a coil reads the value written EARLIER THIS SCAN â€” a shift register MUST compute the next state into temp bits first, then copy temp->state in a LATER network (ascending copy double-sets the wrap bit; descending copy dead-locks at all-zero). A pure-OR network (no series contacts) is driven from an always-ON GVL bool (`xAlwaysOn : BOOL := TRUE;`) â€” the machine-verified form; an empty contacts[] with branches is ALSO the accepted pure-OR form (validator + emitter contract), so pick either; timer pt.constant_value accepts T#500MS literals verbatim and readback echoes them (T#8h also verified, E2E V2 R029). DECLARATION CONTRACT (E2E V2 R029): the generator auto-declares FB INSTANCES only â€” contact/coil/q/pt/pv TARGET variables must be declared by YOU (GVL or variables[]); a missing one compiles to æ²¡æœ‰å®ä¹‰æ ‡è¯†ç¬¦ at the whole-project build while this tool's own diagnostics stay 0. The result lists pouLocalUndeclaredReferences (names not declared in THIS POU's own interface/variables) plus resolvedInGlobalScope (of those, found in a project GVL) and missingEverywhere (in neither) â€” declare the missingEverywhere names before the first build. To add variables to an existing GVL use codesys_pou_add_variable (verified); full declaration rewrites still need delete+recreate. Box networks need NO series contacts â€” enable defaults to TRUE (omit it or pass enable:{name} for gating); a single-output function box may feed its output back into its own input (ADD and SEL both verified: accumulators and hold-latches). ALGORITHMIC WORK (arrays, indexing, loops) is NOT expressible in these network shapes â€” put it in an ST-channel POU (codesys_pou_upsert / codesys_source_import) and keep LAD as the operation/IO layer (E2E V2 R031/R033 verified architecture). A FUNCTION-shaped deliverable maps to a PROGRAM POU whose interface lives in a GVL (VAR_INPUT/VAR_OUTPUT semantics = GVL members, E2E V2 R035 verified: 0/0). VERIFIED SHAPES (E2E V2 R027, 41-network PID at 0/0): a box whose output feeds back into its OWN input of the same name is a legal accumulator (`ADD IN1:=rIAcc -> rIAcc` does rIAcc += term â€” verified by native readback); without a MOVE box, copy a variable with `ADD(IN1:=src, IN2:=rZero)`; analog direct addresses AT %IW0/%QW0 compile 0/0 on the Control Win V3 soft PLC. TABLE INTERPOLATION (E2E V2 R038, 6-segment cam table at 0/0): expand a lookup as an ASCENDING chain of `GE(phase>=P_k)` gated `SEL` segments â€” later segments win (descending order fails: the k=0 leg is always-true and overwrites everything); task call order (task_pou_set pous array order) IS the same-scan data-visibility order, so a MAIN->CAM->OUT chain passes data forward through GVL members in one scan. TIME CONTRACT (E2E V2 R025, 4 compile errors evidence): box DIV/MUL/ADD evaluate DINT/REAL ONLY â€” TIME never participates in arithmetic, there is NO DINT_TO_TIME, and pt accepts only TIME literals or TIME variable names, so LAD ITSELF cannot COMPUTE a period. A variable-PT timer IS usable when the TIME value is computed elsewhere (E2E V2 R036 verified: `pt:{name: tPulsePeriod}` with tPulsePeriod computed in an ST-channel POU, 0/0) â€” for LAD-only variable duty/frequency use the verified pattern instead: a TP timebase (pt = TIME literal) + two CTU counters (PV WORD-typed from the GVL) with the effective timebase = PT + task period compensated by a GVL constant (18 networks, 0/0). The schema's et/cv fields EXIST but are NOT wired (Q only) â€” never plan on reading ET/CV. VERIFIED REGISTRY (real-machine, 142 library instructions + 23 IEC built-in operators, every batch import + readback + precompile 0/0/0, 2026-09-08): 6 FunctionBlocks CTU/CTD/CTUD/TOF/TON/TP; 24 typed comparisons (INT64__EQ/NE/GT/GE/LT/LE, REAL32__*, REAL64__*, UINT64__*...); 28 typed arithmetic (INT32/INT64/REAL32/REAL64/UINT64 __ADD/SUB/MUL/DIV/MOD/ABS; NOTE E2E V2 R034: INT32__ADD answers not_found on live queries on this machine â€” use the built-in ADD operator instead, verified 0/0); 23 typed conversions (X__TO__Y casts + NEW__REAL32__TO__STRING/WSTRING); 9 STANDARD string functions CONCAT/DELETE/FIND/INSERT/LEFT/LEN/MID/REPLACE/RIGHT; 24 typed math (REAL32/REAL64 __SIN/COS/TAN/ASIN/ACOS/ATAN/EXP/EXPT/LN/LOG/SQRT/TRUNC); 4 typed logic (UINT64__AND/OR/XOR/NOT); 14 typed LIMIT/MAX/MIN; 10 typed shifts (UINT32/UINT64/INT32/INT64 __ROL/ROR/SHL/SHR). EXCLUDED (internal/context, each pinned by a real diagnostic): ADDR/ID/MAKE_EVENTID/CODEM*/EVENT*/GETSUPPLIERVERSION/SLOT_ID/SUBSLOT_ID/RESMANINCHARGE/LEN_INTERNAL/MYSTRING_TO_UDINT/MYUDINT_TO_STRING/ANY*__TO__*/multi-output functions. Network kinds: (1) contact_coil: series contacts[] (each {name, negated?} â€” negated=true is the NC contact) + optional branches[] (>=2 parallel OR legs, each {contacts:[...]}) + one coil {target}; semantics: coil = (OR of branch legs) AND (AND of series contacts); branch+NC verified as ONE network on the real machine. (2) box: one Function instruction with port-keyed inputs/outputs maps â€” instruction may be an IEC built-in operator (NOT in the library catalog): compare GT/LT/GE/LE/EQ/NE ports IN1,IN2 -> <the INSTRUCTION NAME>; arithmetic ADD/SUB/MUL/DIV ports IN1,IN2 -> <the INSTRUCTION NAME>; selection SEL (G:BOOL,IN0,IN1), MUX (K,IN0,IN1), LIMIT (MN,IN,MX), MAX/MIN (IN1,IN2); math ABS/SQRT/TRUNC (IN -> <the INSTRUCTION NAME>); conversions INT_TO_REAL/REAL_TO_INT/BOOL_TO_INT/INT_TO_BOOL/WORD_TO_INT/INT_TO_WORD (IN -> <the INSTRUCTION NAME>). The output pin of a box is the instruction name itself, NOT the word 'result' (E2E R027: MUL with outputs.result was rejected, knownPins=[MUL]); read codesys_lad_instruction_signatures when unsure; an instruction with no live catalog or built-in entry is rejected with instruction_signature_unresolved (E2E R032: REAL_TO_DWORD), so pick a name from the registry/list above or query the signatures first â€” or a library instruction from the VERIFIED REGISTRY above whose pins the bridge resolves live. The box is emitted as ONE series rung (contact(enable)->EN); ONLY ONE data output per box (the plugin editor rejects more with 'too many outputs'); string/wstring variables are legal (the emitter writes TC6-legal lowercase string elements). (3) timer: TON/TOF/TP â€” instance + input{name} (BOOL power contact) + pt{constant_value:T#..s|name} + q{name}; v1 emits Q only. (4) counter: CTU/CTD/CTUD â€” instance + input{name} (CU/CD power) + pv + optional reset/load + q{name} (v1: Q only). variables[] = POU local variables {name,type} with IEC primitive types; timer/counter instances are auto-declared (never put FB types in variables[]). Instruction names are validated against the LIVE catalog + the built-in operator table; a rejection carries the exact path + knownPins + remediation. confirm must be generate_project_pou, disposable=true. Requires the vanilla CODESYS project open (the InoProShop line keeps its own tools).
